What the exchange is

A month in Indianapolis for Swiss apprentices. A month in Switzerland for Hoosiers. One paid, U.S.-registered tech apprenticeship — IT, help desk and cybersecurity, with coding and AI on the way — and a skills record that counts on both sides of the Atlantic. Indiana is building its apprenticeship system on the Swiss model; the Crossroads Exchange puts our students inside the original.

Common questions

Before you register

Do I need a degree or experience to start?

No. You start with zero experience in our hands-on Indianapolis lab. Beginners and high-school students are welcome — high-schoolers begin the pre-apprenticeship now and travel at 18.

What does it cost?

Training is free for those who qualify, and you're paid from day one by your Indiana employer once you reach the registered-apprenticeship stage. GI Bill® and VA benefits are accepted. Exchange travel dates, costs and host companies are being finalized with our partners before applications open.

Which tracks are open?

Three DOL-registered tracks are open now — IT support, help desk and cybersecurity — with coding and AI on the way.

Is this a Swiss government program?

No. The Crossroads Exchange is a Hope Training Academy program developed with TIE International (Zürich). It is not a program of the Swiss government.

When does the exchange happen?

The first exchange is planned for May 2027, timed to the Month of May and the 111th Indianapolis 500. Dates, costs and host companies will be confirmed before applications open.
